To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

people’s reactions to different groups are not only qualitatively different in terms of the emotions they elicit and the threats they pose, but that these differences are systematically related to one another, in ways that are predicted by a sociofunctional theory of emotion.

(a) different social groups elicit different profiles of emotion, threat, and their interactions; (b) these emotion and threat profiles are often masked by global measures of prejudice and general threat; and (c) the emotion and threat profiles elicited by different social groups are associated with each other in a manner consistent with the sociofunctional approach.

(a) different groups elicit different emotion profiles, (b) the emotional reactions people feel toward groups are related to specific beliefs about the threats those groups pose, and (c) the emotion and threat profiles of different groups are associated with one another.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of the emotional reactions people feel toward social groups.
the emotional and cognitive processes involved in the perception of social groups.
the nature and origins of prejudice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
prejudice is a functionally relevant emotional response to groups that threaten in-group interests.
the traditional concept of prejudice is not only a misnomer, but also a misdirection.
the authors’ sociofunctional approach provides a powerful framework for understanding the diversity of emotional reactions to different social groups.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
people’s emotional reactions to groups are more complex, and more functionally relevant, than the traditional view of prejudice suggests.

the traditional conception and measurement of prejudice can obscure important information about the nature of prejudice, and a sociofunctional approach can help us to better understand the nature of prejudice and its relationship to other social psychological phenomena.
the traditional conception is not wrong but incomplete.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the emotional reactions to different groups are not uniform.
people’s emotions toward different groups are not a single thing.
the traditional conception that prejudice is a general attitude or evaluative reaction toward a group is too simplistic to capture the complex emotional reactions that different social groups evoke.
